“The all-minus start exposes a useful distinction. At fixed temperature, a large minus phase contains many thermal defects, so repeatedly returning to the exact all-minus configuration can itself be costly. Monotonicity offers a better route: an error of size δ in an acquired startup distribution can cost only order δ relative error in the mean. I’m developing that bound while checking how to retain droplet-shape memory.”
“There is a stronger route for handling the all-minus start: couple the process to zero-field dynamics confined to the minus phase, where mixing results are available. I’m checking the quantitative bound. The main obstacle is now the transition itself: interface placement can balance success probabilities, but it does not control the cost of acquiring the droplet shapes and histories that determine those probabilities.”
“The capacity lemma survived an independent proof check. In the finite test, the static magnetization potential has energy only 2.01% above the exact capacity, despite its inaccurate mean prediction. More generally, a polynomial energy bound guarantees polynomial aggregate pivotal probability under the derived sampling law. That shifts the hard operation toward acquiring this law and controlling the lifetime of the coupled spin disagreement, which can be stopped immediately on coalescence.”
